# MyBrowser MCP installation for agents

MyBrowser has two parts: an MCP server launched by the user's MCP client and an unpacked Chrome extension. Prefer the same-device setup below unless the user explicitly requests remote browser control.

## Same-device setup

1. Add the MCP server to the user's client with this command and arguments:

   ```text
   npx -y @alessai/mybrowser-mcp --ensure-hub --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9009
   ```

2. Restart or reload the MCP client so the server runs once and creates the private local config. `--ensure-hub` keeps the loopback hub alive independently from any one MCP client:

   ```text
   ~/.mybrowser/config.json
   ```

3. On Windows, download `mybrowser-windows-installer.zip` from the latest GitHub release, extract it, and run `install-mybrowser.cmd` without Administrator privileges:

   ```text
   https://github.com/alessai/MyBrowser-MCP/releases/latest
   ```

   The installer verifies the release, installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Alessai\MyBrowser\Extension`, and imports the local port and MCP token without printing or copying the token.

4. Chrome requires one manual trust step that must not be bypassed. Ask the user to open `chrome://extensions`, enable Developer mode, choose Load unpacked, and select:

   ```text
   %LOCALAPPDATA%\Alessai\MyBrowser\Extension
   ```

5. On Linux or macOS, download the latest `mybrowser-extension-*-chrome.zip`, extract it to a stable folder, load that folder unpacked in Chrome, then enter `127.0.0.1`, port `9009`, and the token from `~/.mybrowser/config.json` in the extension popup. Never display the token in chat or logs.

6. Verify the result with MyBrowser's `browser_diagnostics` or `list_browsers` tool. A connected browser must appear before claiming installation succeeded.

## Existing Windows installation

Rerun `install-mybrowser.cmd`. If it updates files, let the user close all Chrome windows when prompted; do not force-kill Chrome. Reopen Chrome and verify the connected extension version with `browser_diagnostics`.

## Safety boundaries

- Do not request Administrator or UAC elevation.
- Do not edit Chrome profile databases, registry policy, or extension storage directly.
- Do not print, echo, copy, or commit the MCP token.
- Do not use `0.0.0.0` for a same-device setup. Remote access requires an explicit user request and a trusted tunnel or network.
- Do not claim Chrome's one-time Load unpacked approval can be automated on ordinary unmanaged Chrome.
- Do not report success until the MCP tool surface can see a connected browser.

Full documentation: https://github.com/alessai/MyBrowser-MCP#readme
